blog_summary: The blog post discusses STTR, a system designed to track all vehicles in real-time by storing their trajectories at the edge of the network. Adrian Colyer highlights the system's ability to manage network bandwidth and storage by processing video locally and storing only vehicle trajectories instead of raw video. The key insights are the pragmatic bounds on storage due to vehicle density and lifetime, and the finite 'activity region' each camera manages. The system uses forward and backward propagation to efficiently track vehicles across multiple cameras, reducing network traffic by lazy trajectory aggregation. While the technology is impressive, the author notes concerns about privacy implications of such pervasive tracking.
paper_title: STTR: A system for tracking all vehicles all the time at the edge of the network
